messages:
maya: heads up — from ~10:02 we saw prefix-cache hit rate collapse from ~82% -> 18% and backend qps jumped x6. latency SLOs breaching. looks cache-related :eyes:
rohit: yikes. pulling graphs now, sending short links. looks like miss surge aligns with the 09:58 deploy by @ci-bot :link:
rohit: hit-rate per model: rtx-default dropped hard, rtx-small less affected. warmup traffic didn't help, saw cache thrash.
ci-bot: deploy: service/runtime v3.6.4 -> v3.7.0 at 09:58 UTC. changelist: tokenizer upgrade + keying normalization tweak. pipeline: canary -> 50% -> 100%.
anil: possible root cause: tokenizer normalization change altered spacing -> cache-key mismatch. new keying removed lowercasing for special tokens. quick diff:
```
- key = model + prefix_text
+ key = model + normalize(prefix_text) // normalization changed token splitting
```
maya: ok immediate action: flip prefix-cache to read-through disabled and fallback to model-local soft cache. running toggle now.
maya: run: `redwoodctl config set runtime.prefix_cache.enabled false --env prod`
opsbot: config: runtime.prefix_cache.enabled set to false for prod by maya at 10:12 UTC. cache-service still warm for ~30s while evictions finish.
rohit: after toggle: backend qps dropped ~55%, latency back within SLO at p95. cache hit-rate reported as ~5% (expected with disables). good stopgap. :thumbsup:
kai: can we avoid complete disable next time? suggests we add a compatibility layer: normalized_key_v{n} and dual-hash reads for a short window. also we should gate tokenizer changes behind cache-key feature flag.
anil: agree. quick mitigation proposal: roll back tokenizer change in runtime and reintroduce normalization as opt-in, plus staggered warmup to avoid stampede. algorithm: bucket prefixes by normalized length and ramp warmup tokens per bucket with jitter.
rohit: profile traces while toggle is in effect: kernel selection looks fine; no GPU stalls. bottleneck was cache-service CPU and thundering connections to backend tokenizer microservice. attaching snippet from perf top:
```
PID   CPU%  FUNC
3212  38.2  kv_cache::handle_get
3212  24.7  tokenize::normalize
```

maya: filing emergency rollback of v3.7.0 to v3.6.4 now. canary already at 0.
ci-bot: rollback initiated at 10:25 UTC, completing...
ci-bot: rollback complete at 10:31 UTC. v3.6.4 serving.
rohit: after rollback + prefix_cache disable: hit-rate slowly climbing as warmup runners populate keys (manual warmup on top queries). backend qps back near baseline.
kai: follow-ups: 1) revert tokenizer change behind feature flag 2) add dual-key read window + migrate 3) implement warmup bucketization (staggered) 4) add cache-service autoscale trigger on miss-rate and connection spikes. I'll own 1+2.
anil: I'll prototype warmup bucketization and safe key migration plan. also add a health-check override: if miss-rate > X for 5m, switch to read-through-only mode automatically (no writes).
maya: good. quick postmortem notes: cause = tokenization/keying regression introduced in deploy -> cache key mismatch -> massive cold misses -> cache-service CPU & backend tokenizer overloaded -> SLO breaches. blast radius amplified by no dual-read migration path and no warmup throttles.
rohit: logs we should archive for postmortem: kv-cache metrics, canary rollout timeline, deploy logs from ci-bot, kernel traces. I'll package charts.
opsbot: reaction :fire: from 10:02-10:30 UTC (incident window).
maya: thanks all. schedule 1hr blameless postmortem tomorrow 11:00; invite: @rohit @anil @kai @infra @oncall. action items: add feature-flag practice, implement dual-key read shim, warmup throttles, autoscale triggers, regenation docs.
rohit: adding follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-9472 (safe-key-migration + dual-read shim).
anil: creating prototype branch for warmup-buckets: will ping when ready for review.
kai: will draft runbook changes for emergency-disable vs rollback decisions.
maya: closing thread. kudos to everyone for fast rollback and mitigation. :raised_hands:
